subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: Talk passes the demo steps to the shared Presentation component. The shared Stage renders their Scene, which composes exported scene-kit nodes; the demo does not recreate presentation orchestration.
evidence: Talk renders Presentation with STEPS.
Scene renders SceneLayer, Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Frame, and Label from the kit.

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: All nine generated steps share one groupKey, and Stage uses it to preserve the grouped Scene mount. Box maps stable demo IDs to Motion layoutId. However, Scene also assigns ENTITY.question and ENTITY.modify to SymbolChip, whose consumer only emits data-presentation-id and supplies no layoutId. The presentation-owned entity IDs therefore do not consistently reach the layout identity mechanism.
evidence: The details array generates nine steps with the same groupKey and Scene.
Stage keys grouped scenes by groupKey.
Box maps id to layoutId; SymbolChip does not.
Scene passes ENTITY.question and ENTITY.modify to SymbolChip.

subcomponents.title: Maintains clear boundaries and scope discipline

criteria.rationale: The required title input is consumed through Talk, Presentation, Header, and Footer. The demo nevertheless declares ENTITY.tray and ENTITY.reveal as stable identities without using either in Scene, leaving dead entries in its identity contract. This is the single code-boundary deduction for that contract.
evidence: Talk supplies a title that Presentation forwards to Header and Footer for rendering.
ENTITY declares tray and reveal, while the complete Scene uses neither.

criteria.rationale: The shared footer and table of contents mark the current item with aria-current and a stable data-presentation-active hook. The demo stylesheet styles those hooks. Presentation defaults attribution on, and the attribution link and its styling are implemented in project-local source.
evidence: Footer progress buttons and Toc entries set semantic current state and active hooks from the current index.
The demo CSS selects the active hooks and styles the attribution link.
Presentation defaults attribution to true; the local Footer renders its default link.

criteria.rationale: The registry loads the demo through its local Talk. Its step data, evolving Scene, identities, and styling reside in the presentation directory. The shared Presentation boundary remains generic over steps and payloads, with no demo-specific branch or duplicated orchestration in Talk.
evidence: The registry maps the demo slug to its local Talk.
Talk delegates to shared Presentation; local steps and Scene contain the demo narrative and entities.
Presentation handles generic navigation, stage, and chrome for supplied steps.

subcomponents.title: Step model, stable identity, and typed boundary

criteria.rationale: Each authored step carries a stable ID, title, and caption; the active step supplies the scene and narration.
evidence: STEPS assigns an ID, title, and caption to each entry; Presentation selects the active step and Footer renders its title and caption.

criteria.rationale: Displayed step numbers come from array positions, so ordering determines numbering.
evidence: Header renders index + 1; Footer maps steps with i + 1 for progress buttons.

criteria.rationale: Presentation passes each step's payload into its Scene, and the sample scene consumes a typed payload.
evidence: Stage renders Scene with payload={step.payload}; STEPS uses Step<SamplePayload> and Scene reads payload.through.

subcomponents.title: Entity transitions and persistent grouped scenes

criteria.rationale: Stable entity IDs feed Motion layout IDs inside a persistent layout group, providing a persisting layout animation path.
evidence: Box assigns layoutId={id}; Stage wraps scenes in LayoutGroup; the sample reuses ENTITY.you and ENTITY.prompt across payload updates.

criteria.rationale: The newcomer primitive waits a fixed delay, while the continuing Box motion does not consume the shared layout timing or expose completion to newcomer entry.
evidence: Appear uses ENTER_DELAY; Box sets layoutId without LAYOUT_T; Stage applies LAYOUT_T only to the scene wrapper's opacity animation.

criteria.rationale: The scene boundary retains a departing whole scene only when its key changes. Ordinary conditional entities inside a grouped scene are removed without a boundary exit mechanism.
evidence: Stage keys grouped scenes by groupKey; Scene conditionally renders entities such as skill and verify without AnimatePresence around those entities.

criteria.rationale: Consecutive steps with the same group key retain the same scene instance while receiving the next payload.
evidence: Stage derives sceneKey from groupKey; the focused test changes steps and asserts updated scene content with mountCount still equal to one.

criteria.rationale: The grouped scene stays mounted, and unconditional child Boxes remain in that scene across payload updates, so their mount entry state does not replay.
evidence: The focused test asserts one scene mount after navigation; Scene renders the you and prompt Boxes unconditionally with stable IDs.

criteria.rationale: The sample uses one grouped Scene that composes persistent entities with payload-dependent additions in a common scene layer.
evidence: All nine STEPS share a group key and Scene; Scene composes the conversation, route row, later nodes, and footnote from payload.through.

subcomponents.title: Present/browse modes, navigation, controls, and boundaries

criteria.rationale: Present mode shows the active step title with the deck title and omits browse narration and table of contents.
evidence: Footer's present branch renders title and step.title; Presentation mounts Toc only in browse mode.

criteria.rationale: Browse mode provides the active title and wrapping caption, a wide-viewport table of contents, previous and next controls, and progress indicators.
evidence: Footer's browse branch renders title, caption, progress, and controls; Presentation renders Toc; the host CSS shows Toc above 760px and sets a caption width without truncation.

criteria.rationale: Mode toggling changes only mode state; the current index remains intact.
evidence: usePresentationNav keeps index and mode in separate states, and toggleMode updates only mode; Presentation uses the retained nav.index.

criteria.rationale: The global key handler advances, reverses, and toggles mode on its supported presentation keys.
evidence: usePresentationNav handles ArrowRight, Space, PageDown, ArrowLeft, PageUp, and p through next, prev, and toggleMode.

criteria.rationale: The swipe handler checks horizontal distance alone; it records neither vertical movement nor touch count, so it cannot reject predominantly vertical or multi-touch gestures.
evidence: Stage forwards only clientX from the first touch; Presentation navigates whenever absolute horizontal delta exceeds 48.

criteria.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents buttons call goTo with a target index.

criteria.rationale: Focused buttons retain Space, but the global handler intercepts supported arrow and page keys while focus remains on an interactive control.
evidence: usePresentationNav exempts only Space for button and link targets; the focused test explicitly sends ArrowRight to a focused Next button and asserts presentation navigation.

criteria.rationale: Moving before the first step is clamped to index zero.
evidence: goTo clamps with Math.max(0, ...); the focused test clicks Previous at the first step and asserts index 0.

criteria.rationale: Moving beyond the last step is clamped to the last valid index.
evidence: goTo caps at count - 1; the focused test advances from the last step and asserts index 1 remains active.

subcomponents.title: Style ownership, hooks, framework neutrality, and attribution

criteria.rationale: Kit markup exposes stable hooks for the root, stage, scene, controls, active entries, and attribution.
evidence: Presentation, Stage, Footer, and Toc emit data-presentation-* attributes on their rendered elements.

criteria.rationale: The rendered kit supplies structure, positioning, content, interaction hooks, and animation, but no kit-owned colors, backgrounds, borders, shadows, or decorative typography. The presentation imports its own stylesheet, which supplies those visual treatments. The bootstrap stylesheet likewise contains structural rules only.
evidence: Presentation renders Header, Toc, Stage, and Footer; their markup supplies content and hooks without inline visual styling.
All eight exported scene primitives were inspected. They pass through caller styles or classes, or add only structural positioning and animation.
The kit stylesheet defines layout and positioning. The sample presentation stylesheet defines the palette, type, borders, backgrounds, and control appearance.

criteria.rationale: The rendered kit and sample use React components and plain CSS without requiring a styling framework.
evidence: Talk imports its own style.css; kit components expose className and style hooks; package dependencies include no CSS framework.

criteria.rationale: Authored scenes can place diagram entities at explicit coordinates within the fixed canvas.
evidence: Scene positions Boxes with left and top styles and composes arrows and other nodes; sample CSS positions the route, connectors, and overlays within the canvas.

criteria.rationale: The kit emits a default link, but its bottom-right placement comes from host-owned CSS rather than kit markup or kit-owned positioning.
evidence: Footer renders the attribution anchor without positioning; src/index.css supplies position:absolute, right, and bottom, which the sample CSS later adjusts.

criteria.rationale: The attribution has stable class and data hooks that presentation-owned CSS can target.
evidence: Footer emits presentation-attribution and data-presentation-attribution; sample style.css targets that class.

criteria.rationale: The header renders a brand only when the host supplies one; the default attribution remains a separate footer element.
evidence: Header conditionally renders brand from its prop; Presentation forwards the optional brand; the focused test asserts no default brand link.

evidence: The sole bootstrap integration case starts with a fresh target and copies the full bootstrap; the skill's instruction to use an anchored app as-is has no corresponding scaffold-branch test.

criteria.rationale: No focused executable evidence constructs a partially scaffolded host and verifies that only missing contracts are added while existing ones are preserved.
evidence: The bootstrap integration case copies the complete template into a fresh target; it does not set up an existing build, kit, or registry anchor before scaffolding.

criteria.rationale: The materialized bootstrap is checked for style-neutral host and kit CSS, and the inspected host CSS contains structural rules without a palette or typography scheme.
evidence: The bootstrap test asserts the copied host CSS and kit files lack specified color, font, shadow, and border declarations; the bootstrap host CSS defines structural placement rules.

criteria.rationale: The executable test derives the template path from the repository root, so it does not verify resolution from the skill file's containing directory.
evidence: bootstrapSource is formed with repositoryRoot and a hardcoded repository-relative skill path. The skill states the intended skill-relative rule, but no focused test exercises that resolution.

criteria.rationale: No focused executable evidence sets up a monorepo, selects its presentations app, or checks that root files remain intact and dependencies install in the selected app.
evidence: The bootstrap test creates only a temporary app path; it has no workspace manifest, packages or apps structure, or monorepo target assertion.

criteria.rationale: The fresh bootstrap test does not exercise target selection for an existing standalone project root.
evidence: The test assigns appRoot directly and copies the template there; it does not construct a standalone project and assert that its root is selected.

criteria.rationale: No focused executable or workflow evidence exercises an ambiguous nonempty target, records confirmation, and verifies the chosen mutation.
evidence: The only scaffold test uses a fresh target and contains no nonempty project setup or confirmation branch.

criteria.rationale: The skill requires unique slug registration, and the registry and router implement slug-based loading.
evidence: The skill directs registration in the presentation index; resolveRoute finds the matching entry by slug, Router passes that entry to RouteLoader, and the route test asserts registered-slug resolution.

criteria.rationale: The skill assigns visual treatment to presentation-owned CSS, and the presentation template imports its own stylesheet.
evidence: The skill directs colors, type, spacing, layout, and component treatment into presentation CSS; the template Talk imports ./style.css, while the bootstrap host CSS supplies structural rules.

criteria.rationale: The skill explicitly requires preserving existing routes and presentations, and registry routing can load entries independently.
evidence: The creation instructions require a unique slug, one new registration, and preservation of every existing route and presentation; resolveRoute selects an entry by its slug.

criteria.rationale: The skill requires resolving an ambiguous modification target before editing.
evidence: For a modification without an unambiguous name, it directs the agent to list registered presentations and ask which one to change before editing.

criteria.rationale: The skill confines modification work to the selected presentation and the minimum necessary host changes.
evidence: The modification instruction requires focused edits to requested steps, entities, or style and preservation of other steps and unrelated presentations.

subcomponents.title: Self-verification and fixing failures before completion

criteria.rationale: The skill makes build, render, browser, and screenshot inspection checks part of its completion gate.
evidence: Its verification section requires build and render checks, opening the route in a real browser, capturing screenshots, and reviewing the actual screenshots before reporting completion.

criteria.rationale: The skill explicitly requires fixing failures and rerunning checks before success.
evidence: It says to fix and rerun build and render failures, rerun inspection after fixes, and withhold completion while build, render, or visual inspection has an unresolved failure.

subcomponents.title: Detects a missing reference sample

subcomponents.title: Preview addressing and runtime/step error detection

criteria.rationale: Preview binding, readiness requests, and browser navigation use the same IPv4 loopback host.
evidence: Both preview commands pass host 127.0.0.1; each script builds its readiness and browser URL from that host.

criteria.rationale: Readiness does not conclusively establish that the responder is the spawned child, and the verifier does not fail if that child exits after its exit-code check.
evidence: The loop checks preview.exitCode before fetch, then accepts any successful response at the fixed port. It does not recheck the child after fetch or during browser traversal.

criteria.rationale: The verifier collects console and page errors, but focused executable evidence covers only a console error; no cited test exercises a page error and verifies its failing step.
evidence: The console-fault test injects console.error and asserts the step-1 failure. No pageerror injection or assertion appears in the focused failure tests.

criteria.rationale: A focused test stalls navigation and verifies a nonzero outcome that identifies the failed step.
evidence: The stalled-transition test replaces the navigation update, runs verification, and asserts nonzero exit plus 'step 2: data-step-index did not advance'.

subcomponents.title: Complete, settled screenshot capture

criteria.rationale: An implemented project-local inspect command starts a preview, opens the requested route in Playwright, and writes screenshots.
evidence: The package inspect script invokes inspect-presentation.mjs; that script launches Chromium and calls page.screenshot for each step.

criteria.rationale: The executable test proves two screenshot files were written, but does not establish that each file depicts its intended step from the intended preview.
evidence: The integration test asserts the capture message and nonempty step-01.png and step-02.png files. It does not assert rendered step identity or preview provenance for either image.

criteria.rationale: Capture uses a fixed 900 ms wait without observing animation completion or consuming the transition contract used by scene motion.
evidence: The helper calls page.waitForTimeout(900) before screenshots. Runtime motion consumes LAYOUT_T and Appear consumes ENTER_T and ENTER_DELAY, none of which the helper reads.

evidence: Warning names use class or node attributes, not span text. The test's absence assertion searches for 'intentional one' or 'intentional two', strings that cannot appear in those wa…

criteria.rationale: The diagnostic compares rendered active and inactive styles, and a browser test asserts both warning messages when those styles match.
evidence: compare reads computed color, background, border, and weight for active and inactive progress and table-of-contents entries. The test gives each pair identical styles and asserts both warnings.

criteria.rationale: The browser test verifies the default-style warning only; focused executable evidence for missing and undersized attribution warnings is absent.
evidence: The test supplies a browser-default attribution link and asserts that warning. It has no missing-attribution or undersized-attribution setup and assertion.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk passes the demo steps to the shared Presentation component. The shared Stage renders their Scene, which composes exported scene-kit nodes; the demo does not recreate presentation orchestration.
evidence: Talk renders Presentation with STEPS.
Scene renders SceneLayer, Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Frame, and Label from the kit.

demo-integration.rationale: All nine generated steps share one groupKey, and Stage uses it to preserve the grouped Scene mount. Box maps stable demo IDs to Motion layoutId. However, Scene also assigns ENTITY.question and ENTITY.modify to SymbolChip, whose consumer only emits data-presentation-id and supplies no layoutId. The presentation-owned entity IDs therefore do not consistently reach the layout identity mechanism.
evidence: The details array generates nine steps with the same groupKey and Scene.
Stage keys grouped scenes by groupKey.
Box maps id to layoutId; SymbolChip does not.
Scene passes ENTITY.question and ENTITY.modify to SymbolChip.

demo-integration.rationale: The required title input is consumed through Talk, Presentation, Header, and Footer. The demo nevertheless declares ENTITY.tray and ENTITY.reveal as stable identities without using either in Scene, leaving dead entries in its identity contract. This is the single code-boundary deduction for that contract.
evidence: Talk supplies a title that Presentation forwards to Header and Footer for rendering.
ENTITY declares tray and reveal, while the complete Scene uses neither.

demo-integration.rationale: The shared footer and table of contents mark the current item with aria-current and a stable data-presentation-active hook. The demo stylesheet styles those hooks. Presentation defaults attribution on, and the attribution link and its styling are implemented in project-local source.
evidence: Footer progress buttons and Toc entries set semantic current state and active hooks from the current index.
The demo CSS selects the active hooks and styles the attribution link.
Presentation defaults attribution to true; the local Footer renders its default link.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry loads the demo through its local Talk. Its step data, evolving Scene, identities, and styling reside in the presentation directory. The shared Presentation boundary remains generic over steps and payloads, with no demo-specific branch or duplicated orchestration in Talk.
evidence: The registry maps the demo slug to its local Talk.
Talk delegates to shared Presentation; local steps and Scene contain the demo narrative and entities.
Presentation handles generic navigation, stage, and chrome for supplied steps.

scene-kit.rationale: Each authored step carries a stable ID, title, and caption; the active step supplies the scene and narration.
evidence: STEPS assigns an ID, title, and caption to each entry; Presentation selects the active step and Footer renders its title and caption.

scene-kit.rationale: Displayed step numbers come from array positions, so ordering determines numbering.
evidence: Header renders index + 1; Footer maps steps with i + 1 for progress buttons.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation passes each step's payload into its Scene, and the sample scene consumes a typed payload.
evidence: Stage renders Scene with payload={step.payload}; STEPS uses Step<SamplePayload> and Scene reads payload.through.

scene-kit.rationale: Stable entity IDs feed Motion layout IDs inside a persistent layout group, providing a persisting layout animation path.
evidence: Box assigns layoutId={id}; Stage wraps scenes in LayoutGroup; the sample reuses ENTITY.you and ENTITY.prompt across payload updates.

scene-kit.rationale: The newcomer primitive waits a fixed delay, while the continuing Box motion does not consume the shared layout timing or expose completion to newcomer entry.
evidence: Appear uses ENTER_DELAY; Box sets layoutId without LAYOUT_T; Stage applies LAYOUT_T only to the scene wrapper's opacity animation.

scene-kit.rationale: The scene boundary retains a departing whole scene only when its key changes. Ordinary conditional entities inside a grouped scene are removed without a boundary exit mechanism.
evidence: Stage keys grouped scenes by groupKey; Scene conditionally renders entities such as skill and verify without AnimatePresence around those entities.

scene-kit.rationale: Consecutive steps with the same group key retain the same scene instance while receiving the next payload.
evidence: Stage derives sceneKey from groupKey; the focused test changes steps and asserts updated scene content with mountCount still equal to one.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped scene stays mounted, and unconditional child Boxes remain in that scene across payload updates, so their mount entry state does not replay.
evidence: The focused test asserts one scene mount after navigation; Scene renders the you and prompt Boxes unconditionally with stable IDs.

scene-kit.rationale: The sample uses one grouped Scene that composes persistent entities with payload-dependent additions in a common scene layer.
evidence: All nine STEPS share a group key and Scene; Scene composes the conversation, route row, later nodes, and footnote from payload.through.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode shows the active step title with the deck title and omits browse narration and table of contents.
evidence: Footer's present branch renders title and step.title; Presentation mounts Toc only in browse mode.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode provides the active title and wrapping caption, a wide-viewport table of contents, previous and next controls, and progress indicators.
evidence: Footer's browse branch renders title, caption, progress, and controls; Presentation renders Toc; the host CSS shows Toc above 760px and sets a caption width without truncation.

scene-kit.rationale: Mode toggling changes only mode state; the current index remains intact.
evidence: usePresentationNav keeps index and mode in separate states, and toggleMode updates only mode; Presentation uses the retained nav.index.

scene-kit.rationale: The global key handler advances, reverses, and toggles mode on its supported presentation keys.
evidence: usePresentationNav handles ArrowRight, Space, PageDown, ArrowLeft, PageUp, and p through next, prev, and toggleMode.

scene-kit.rationale: The swipe handler checks horizontal distance alone; it records neither vertical movement nor touch count, so it cannot reject predominantly vertical or multi-touch gestures.
evidence: Stage forwards only clientX from the first touch; Presentation navigates whenever absolute horizontal delta exceeds 48.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents buttons call goTo with a target index.
evidence: Footer progress buttons call goTo(i); Toc entries call goTo(i); the focused test clicks the second progress button and asserts index 1.

scene-kit.rationale: Active progress and contents entries expose semantic current state and stable active hooks.
evidence: Footer sets aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active; Toc sets aria-current='location' and the active hook; the focused test asserts both.

scene-kit.rationale: Focused buttons retain Space, but the global handler intercepts supported arrow and page keys while focus remains on an interactive control.
evidence: usePresentationNav exempts only Space for button and link targets; the focused test explicitly sends ArrowRight to a focused Next button and asserts presentation navigation.

scene-kit.rationale: Moving before the first step is clamped to index zero.
evidence: goTo clamps with Math.max(0, ...); the focused test clicks Previous at the first step and asserts index 0.

scene-kit.rationale: Moving beyond the last step is clamped to the last valid index.
evidence: goTo caps at count - 1; the focused test advances from the last step and asserts index 1 remains active.

scene-kit.rationale: Although the canvas uses one scale factor, the fit calculation includes stage padding and can leave the canvas clipped at an ordinary viewport width.
evidence: source audit: src/presentation-kit/useFitScale.ts measures the stage&#39;s bounding rectangle; src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx sizes the frame from that scale.

source audit: src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/style.css gives the stage 2rem horizontal padding, while src/index.css sets box-sizing: border-box and overflow: hidden. At a 900px stage wi…

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered authored canvas consumes 880×380 defaults.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Stage uses both as the canvas width and height.

scene-kit.rationale: Kit markup exposes stable hooks for the root, stage, scene, controls, active entries, and attribution.
evidence: Presentation, Stage, Footer, and Toc emit data-presentation-* attributes on their rendered elements.

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered kit supplies structure, positioning, content, interaction hooks, and animation, but no kit-owned colors, backgrounds, borders, shadows, or decorative typography. The presentation imports its own stylesheet, which supplies those visual treatments. The bootstrap stylesheet likewise contains structural rules only.
evidence: Presentation renders Header, Toc, Stage, and Footer; their markup supplies content and hooks without inline visual styling.
All eight exported scene primitives were inspected. They pass through caller styles or classes, or add only structural positioning and animation.
The kit stylesheet defines layout and positioning. The sample presentation stylesheet defines the palette, type, borders, backgrounds, and control appearance.

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered kit and sample use React components and plain CSS without requiring a styling framework.
evidence: Talk imports its own style.css; kit components expose className and style hooks; package dependencies include no CSS framework.

scene-kit.rationale: Authored scenes can place diagram entities at explicit coordinates within the fixed canvas.
evidence: Scene positions Boxes with left and top styles and composes arrows and other nodes; sample CSS positions the route, connectors, and overlays within the canvas.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit emits a default link, but its bottom-right placement comes from host-owned CSS rather than kit markup or kit-owned positioning.
evidence: Footer renders the attribution anchor without positioning; src/index.css supplies position:absolute, right, and bottom, which the sample CSS later adjusts.

scene-kit.rationale: The attribution has stable class and data hooks that presentation-owned CSS can target.
evidence: Footer emits presentation-attribution and data-presentation-attribution; sample style.css targets that class.

scene-kit.rationale: The header renders a brand only when the host supplies one; the default attribution remains a separate footer element.
evidence: Header conditionally renders brand from its prop; Presentation forwards the optional brand; the focused test asserts no default brand link.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill directs the agent to proceed without redundant questions when the prompt has enough detail.

evidence: The bootstrap integration case copies the complete template into a fresh target; it does not set up an existing build, kit, or registry anchor before scaffolding.

evidence: The bootstrap test creates only a temporary app path; it has no workspace manifest, packages or apps structure, or monorepo target assertion.

presentation-skill.rationale: The fresh bootstrap test does not exercise target selection for an existing standalone project root.
evidence: The test assigns appRoot directly and copies the template there; it does not construct a standalone project and assert that its root is selected.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused executable or workflow evidence exercises an ambiguous nonempty target, records confirmation, and verifies the chosen mutation.
evidence: The only scaffold test uses a fresh target and contains no nonempty project setup or confirmation branch.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires unique slug registration, and the registry and router implement slug-based loading.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill assigns visual treatment to presentation-owned CSS, and the presentation template imports its own stylesheet.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill confines modification work to the selected presentation and the minimum necessary host changes.
evidence: The modification instruction requires focused edits to requested steps, entities, or style and preservation of other steps and unrelated presentations.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill makes build, render, browser, and screenshot inspection checks part of its completion gate.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires fixing failures and rerunning checks before success.
